messages:
marta: Heads-up—since ~03:00 UTC we've been seeing intermittent GPU attach failures in the scratchpool across us-west1. Provisioning jobs timeout with mount i/o errors.
ryan: Got a few gnodes from the logs: gnode-143, gnode-198, gnode-211. dmesg shows repeated NVME I/O timeouts and reassignments. Reallocated sector count ticked up on 143.
anika: Pasting relevant snippet from gnode-143 (`dmesg -T | tail -n 40`):
```
[Thu Mar 21 03:14:02] nvme0: I/O 12345 QID 4 timeout, aborting
[Thu Mar 21 03:14:02] nvme0: timeout waiting for completion
[Thu Mar 21 03:14:03] nvme0: reassigning LBA range, reallocated_sector_count +1
[Thu Mar 21 03:14:07] blk_update_request: I/O error, dev nvme0n1, sector 1052672
```
ryan: Also correlates with ephemeral-cleaner runs — heavy scrub passes started at 03:12. Cleaner concurrency seems high.
marta: @ryan can you check if scrub windows line up with batch GPU launches? worried about scheduling overlap.
ryan: Yes — batch scheduler kicked at 03:10 for a large training fleet scale-up. Lots of small writes + scrub => iops headroom exhausted.
sre-bot: [alert] nvme_reassign_threshold crossed on gnode-143, severity: warning.
dev-gor: My guess: noise-floor IOPS from concurrent scrubs + small-file churn causes controller queuing; persistent writes hit reassign threshold and drive starts cycling.
anika: Quick mitigation: reduce cleaner concurrency from 12 -> 4 and stagger scrub start times across azs. Example patch I tested on one canary node: `PATCH scrub-config: concurrency: 4, window: 03:30-04:30, jitter: 6m`
marta: Nice. @sam can you canary that config in us-west1 (5 nodes) and watch for attach success rate, iowait, and SMART counters?
sam: Starting rollout to 5 canary nodes now. Will keep payload low and monitor for 45m.
ops-jen: Cost note: replacing a handful of NVME drives would be ~ $6k + downtime per rack. If config tweaks reduce reassigns we save immediate spend. But tracked SMART growth on some nodes suggests some replacement in next quarter.
ryan: Agreed. Short term: throttle scrub concurrency + enable per-node iosched limits (blkio cgroup) for cleaner process. Medium: add a low-latency scrub mode in the cleaner to favor read-heavy checks over aggressive writes.
dev-gor: We can also add a quick safeguard: when reassign count increases > N within T, auto-deprioritize that node for GPU attaches for 30m. Low-risk fallback.
anika: I pushed the scrub concurrency patch to `staging` and a small QoS change to `ops/configs/blkio-scrub.toml`. Command used for throttling: `echo 500 > /sys/fs/cgroup/blkio/cleaner/blkio.throttle.read_iops_device`
marta: Sam, any early results?
sam: Canary looks good so far. Attach success up from 86% -> 98% on the 5 nodes. iowait dropped ~60%. SMART reassign counters stable for now. I'll extend to 20 nodes if no regressions in 30m.
ops-jen: If canary holds, ops proposal: roll config asap and then schedule a replacement plan for drives with sustained SMART growth — priority below critical compute racks. Communicate to finance for CAPEX forecast.
marta: Plan: 1) Complete canary to 20 nodes (sam) 2) Roll concurrency + blkio QoS cluster-wide (ryan/dev-gor) 3) Add auto-deprioritize heuristic (dev-gor) 4) Track SMART deltas and schedule replacements next quarter (ops-jen). I'll open a follow-up ticket and ping customer success if SLA windows impacted.
ryan: I'll also add a short dashboard showing reassign_count vs attach_fail rate per node to help operations.
anika: Leaving the patch links here: https://git.internal/ops/cleaner/+/reduce-concurrency and https://git.internal/ops/configs/blkio-scrub.toml
marta: Thanks all — marking as active incident until rollouts complete. :thumbsup:
